findings.title: Scrubbed PATH does not say how the agent runtime's executables are reached
findings.description:
- **Gap:** D7 limits `PATH` to the adapter entries, `<id>.home/bin` (only `git` and `uv`) and the system directories, and explicitly drops `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew, pipx and uv tool installs. Those are the usual homes of the agent CLIs, `node` and `cf`, and the design never says whether the dispatch path needs any of them on `PATH`.
- **Consequence for the auth check:** D8's probe would report a missing binary as an auth `no`. The architecture's question ("whether the agent's auth still works with its config directory redirected") would then be answered wrongly.
- **Consequence for 424:** the slice plan has 424 consume this environment unchanged for `sq run`, so it inherits the same gap.
- **Fix:** list the runtime executables each profile needs. Either add them to `HARNESS_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` or state that the runtime resolves them without `PATH`. Give the probe a distinct result for "runtime not found" versus "auth failed".

findings.title: Install failure reasons have no case for network or build failure
findings.description:
- **Gap:** the install step is a new network I/O path, but `EnvironmentFailureReason` has only `no_lockfile`, `lockfile_unsupported`, `lock_stale_or_unresolvable`, `install_timeout` and `installer_missing`. A dropped connection, an index outage or a failed sdist build has nowhere to go except `lock_stale_or_unresolvable`.
- **Why it matters:** the architecture says "a lockfile that no longer resolves disqualifies the case", and 422's yield report counts exclusions per reason. A transient outage would be recorded as a permanent property of the case, which defeats "Absent is not zero".
- **Fix:** add a reason for install failures that are not attributable to the lock (or an explicit `install_failed` catch-all), and state how uv's output maps to each reason.
- **Related criterion:** line 308 and walkthrough step 5 require that a stale lock leaves no `.venv`. I believe `uv sync --locked` creates the environment before it validates the lock; if so, the criterion cannot pass as written. Either confirm uv's ordering or reword it to "the sandbox is removed".

findings.title: `EnvironmentIdentity` placement conflicts with the stated dependency direction
findings.description:
- **Conflict:** line 97 says `metrology/` does not depend on `benchmark/`. But `EnvironmentIdentity` is defined in `benchmark/adapter.py`, and line 119 says 422's qualification records and 424's replay records carry it. Those are store payloads under D3, in `metrology/benchmark_models.py`.
- **Consequence:** 422 must either import `benchmark/` from `metrology/` or duplicate the model. The same applies to `FailureKind` if qualification records store it.
- **Fix:** decide here, since this slice owns the seam. Either put the persisted value types in `metrology/benchmark_models.py`, or state that records carry only `identity_digest` and plain strings.

findings.title: Case sets are not keyed on `ProjectId`, and the replacement keying is under-specified
findings.description:
- **Deviation:** the architecture ("optional sibling payloads, no migration, keyed on `ProjectId`") and the 421 plan entry both key new records on `ProjectId`. D2 keys `CaseSet` by a global name instead.
- **What holds up:** the pooling rationale is sound, and the deviation is stated openly.
- **What is missing:**
  - What the `MetrologyRecord` envelope's project field holds for a `case_set` record.
  - How existing per-project queries treat that record.
  - What stops two projects that reuse a name from silently versioning each other's set, since `write_case_set` would write v2 of the other project's set.
- **Fix:** specify the envelope value, and either scope the name (for example an optional project qualifier) or reject a write whose case ids share no project with the previous version.

findings.title: Sandbox tree sits two directories from the store that now holds the answers
findings.description: `~/.config/squadron/benchmark/<id>/` is a sibling of `metrology/`, which after this slice holds `reference_sha` and the hidden test ids for the case being replayed. Redirecting `HOME` does not hide a relative `../../metrology`. D4 acknowledges this and defers to 424's scan, which matches the architecture's "directory, not a jail" position and 177's precedent. 424 should treat the path as a required scan entry.

findings.title: Scope matches the slice plan entry
findings.description:
- All four planned items are present: records, environment resolution, scrubbed environment with auth check, and the adapter seam with the suite runner.
- Discovery, fairness, injection, leak scan and grading are correctly excluded to 422–425.
- Both "open for slice design" questions are answered: lockfile-less projects in D5 and the adapter shape in D9.
- The single-entry registry, the two CLI verification commands and the three timeout keys are each used by this slice's own success criteria. Nothing is cuttable.

findings.title: Case identity and immutability
findings.description:
- The identity covers the architecture's fields plus the exclusion list the slice plan requires.
- Adding `reference_sha` is justified, because hidden-test source is read from the reference.
- Tamper rejection on read fails explicitly and never yields a second case under an old id.
- Set versions are never rewritten.

findings.title: Scrubbed environment follows the leak principle
findings.description:
- Building from an allowlist, redirecting `HOME`, seeding without store or memory, and ordering `PATH` so the start commit's `sq` wins all implement the architecture's "answer stays out of reach" principle.
- `scrub_spec_version` in the environment identity satisfies the requirement that qualification runs in the same environment as replays.
- Auth failure is reported and never worked around.

findings.title: Suite runner classification supports the fairness rule
findings.description:
- The kinds separate the architecture's test-first disqualifiers (collection error, import error, module `AttributeError`, missing patch target) from the qualifying ones (assertion, project exception).
- `other_exception` sends ambiguous cases to "excluded with that reason, never admitted".
- Timeout, missing JSONL and old pytest each have an explicit, non-silent outcome.

findings.title: Store extension and sandbox extraction
findings.description:
- Records are sibling payloads with no schema bump or migration, as the architecture requires.
- `HistoryFreeSandbox` is extracted by composition, and `ReplaySandbox`'s surface and tests are unchanged. That reuses 177 without forking it.

structured_findings.summary: Scrubbed PATH does not say how the agent runtime's executables are reached
Install failure reasons have no case for network or build failure
`EnvironmentIdentity` placement conflicts with the stated dependency direction
Case sets are not keyed on `ProjectId`, and the replacement keying is under-specified
Sandbox tree sits two directories from the store that now holds the answers
Scope matches the slice plan entry
Scrubbed environment follows the leak principle
Suite runner classification supports the fairness rule
